description: Fig. 12 is a single schematic (no photos, spectra or axes) drawn as three sequential stages read left to right and connected by thick black arrows, illustrating the TRIP effect as a deformation mechanism. A long salmon-coloured arrow runs across the top, labelled "Increasing Strain values (ε)", and a blue arrow across the bottom is labelled "Deformation induced martensite formed inside austenite (TRIP)". Left stage: a large pale-pink hexagon labelled γc (coarse austenite) adjacent to a white hexagon labelled α (ferrite) and a smaller orange hexagon labelled γf; short red arrows are drawn at the α/γ boundary, which the caption states represent partitioning of Mn from ferrite to austenite. Middle stage: the γc region has become a hatched hexagon labelled α′, while γf and α still carry "⊥" dislocation-glide symbols. Right stage: γf itself becomes hatched (partially transformed to α′), retaining dislocation symbols, so both austenite types end as martensite. Two legend boxes below read "γc : Undergoing TRIP (becoming α′)" and "γf : Undergoing dislocation glide followed by TRIP". The panel legend (through the citing text) assigns the coarse, lower-Mn/C grains the earlier transformation, providing high work hardening at low strain, and the finer, higher-Mn/C grains the later transformation.
measured_quantities: strain value (ε), qualitative increasing direction only
product of strength and elongation (PSE, GPa%) as reported in the citing text

observations.observation: The figure is a three-stage schematic joined by black arrows, with an orange top arrow labelled 'Increasing Strain values (ε)' spanning left to right.
A blue bottom arrow is labelled 'Deformation induced martensite formed inside austenite (TRIP)'.
Phase/grain labels printed in the schematic are γc (large pale-pink hexagon), γf (smaller orange hexagon), α (white hexagon) and α′ (hatched hexagon).
Dislocation-glide symbols (⊥) are drawn inside γf and α in the middle stage, and inside γf in the right stage, indicating dislocation glide as an additional deformation mode.
Legend boxes read 'γc : Undergoing TRIP (becoming α′)' and 'γf : Undergoing dislocation glide followed by TRIP'.

The caption states that the red arrows in the first stage represent the partitioning of Mn from ferrite to austenite; the arrows themselves are small red strokes clustered at the α/γc boundary and their direction of Mn flux is not resolvable from the pixels alone.
The citing text identifies two austenite types: coarser γc with relatively lower Mn and C concentration, and finer γf with relatively higher Mn and C concentration.

The citing text states that coarser γc grains transform to martensite earlier during deformation (lower mechanical stability, high work hardening at low strain) while finer γf grains transform later (higher mechanical stability, constant work hardening during continuous TRIP).
The citing text reports PSE values of 61 GPa% for sample M1 and 41 GPa% for sample M2, with M1's higher value attributed to its higher austenite fraction.
No numeric data values, scale bars or axis ticks are printed anywhere in this schematic; the only quantitative element is the qualitative 'Increasing Strain values (ε)' arrow.

subfigures.description: First strain stage: a large pale-pink hexagon labelled γc alongside a white hexagon labelled α and a smaller orange hexagon labelled γf; short red arrows at the α/γc boundary are stated by the caption to represent Mn partitioning from ferrite to austenite.
Intermediate strain stage: the γc hexagon has transformed into a hatched (martensitic) hexagon labelled α′, while γf and the α region remain with '⊥' dislocation-glide symbols.
High-strain stage: the γf hexagon is now also hatched and transformed to α′, still showing dislocation symbols, so both austenite types have become martensite.
Two captioned boxes: 'γc : Undergoing TRIP (becoming α′)' and 'γf : Undergoing dislocation glide followed by TRIP'.
